M O R E   M A I L ! !

      May, 1992      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Alan D. Cox..........03    15

 Kevin Cooper.........21    27

 Malcolm Perry........31    43

 Marc Broster.........44    49

 Dave Marriott........50    51

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Alan D. Cox, DYFED

Dear Brian

Some points for the information
of your readers and comments on
OUTLET Issue No. 56.

Following the comments by Mr.
Ottery in the last OUTLET about
SAM/PC transfer software, I sent
off for SAM Supplement Issue 7.
The programs there were only for
transferring PC to SAM, which is
relatively easy, given the
Disciple/SAM command READ AT
etc. The programs did not cover
the reverse situation, which
seems to me more difficult since
I do not know the PC (BASIC?)
equivalent of READ AT etc.

However, it appears that there
are PD/Shareware programs
available from the PC end and I
am helping one of the members of
my local Computer Group
investigate them.

It might be worth mentioning
that following a suggestion that
I made, SAMCo (Charles Gill)
came to a recent meeting of my
local computer club, the
Carmarthen Computer User Group,
and gave a useful presentation
on the present state and future
prospects for SAM. Clearly,
being so close to their home
base made this relatively easy
for them to do, but if anyone
else is interested in a similar
presentation it would be
worthwhile contacting SAMCo.

Following my query recently
about the use of CHR$(19) with
the Tandy CGP-115, I received a
very helpful letter from Dr. Tom
Wilson of Falkirk and we sub-
sequently spoke on the phone. As
a result of this and some sub-
sequent research I did, it seems
I can, perhaps, refine my
question. The facts are these.
In the CGP manual there are
several sample demonstration
programs and the most elaborate
of these, which draws pie charts
and sine/cosine curves, includes
the command LPRINT CHR$(19).

I've been driving the CGP using
my EPSON HX20, partly because it
seemed appropriate to couple
together two contemporary pieces

of machinery - they both date
from the early 80s - and partly
because I was looking for a
printer for the EPSON - it only
has a serial output and my other
printers only have parallel
input (the CGP has both as
standard) - and this uses an
EPSON/Microsoft BASIC. Unless I
use CHR$(19) I do not get the
right response.


However, one of Dr. Tom Wilson's
comments was that although he
had successfully used his CGP
with his Spectrum/Disciple set-
up and the serial output, he had
had no success with his SAM and
the MGT comms interface using
the serial port.

I suggested to him that he would
do better using the parallel
port (with a printer switch if
he wanted to keep the CGP and
his LC-20 connected up at the
same time). My reason for saying
this was that I was only too
aware of the complications of
setting up serial links having
fought the battle before I
linked the CGP and the HX20.
Before I recommended this, I had
proved to myself that I could
drive the CGP from SAM using the
FORMAT parallel printer inter-
face (and I assume that this is
standard CENTRONICS). This
proved OK, but in the process I
also found that using SAM, and
this interface, with SAM BASIC,
I did not need CHR$(19) in order
to get proper output!

So where am I? Is it that
CHR$(19) is something to do with
driving the serial input to the
CGP? or is it something to do
with EPSON/Microsoft BASIC? I
have written to Tandy, who are
normally very helpful in
response to problems such as
this, and they say that they are
as baffled as I am. Following
their suggestion, I have written
to Radio Shack/Tandy in the USA:
I will, of course, let you know
if this resolves the problem.

Thank you for your comments on
OUTDEX and SC_ASSEMBLER in this
month's OUTLET. I will follow up
your suggestions - which I am
sure others will also find
useful - and let you know in due

course whether I have been
successful (and it is no good
making remarks like 'as clever
as you' - I do not respond to
such blatant flattery!). I note
that you offer no comments on
the apparent misinformation on
the disk controller in SAM - has
Brian Gaff any comments?


I note your comments on the
reverse listing crash, which you
get with LIST FORMAT. May I
suggest that you have another
look at my comments, quoting
Andy Wright, in OUTLET 54,
Add-Enders, More Mail 1, which
covers your case, I think and
gives a solution.

Re: Matthew Weedall's query on 2
Mbyte drives - this is covered
in the current SAMCo Newsdisk.

I note, and agree with, your
comments on MasterBasic and
MasterDOS - obviously Andy
Wright is entitled to due reward
from his efforts, so I agree
that SAMCo ought to buy him out
so that MasterBasic/DOS are
available to all.

I normally FORMAT new disks as
soon as I get them and then add
DOS - but of course I need to
keep two different sets now, so
that I do not inadvertently send
someone MasterBasic, which of
course is combined with SAMDOS.

On this general point, I find
that MasterBASIC uses areas of
the memory that SAMBASIC did not
- not surprisingly, of course -
so that for example, the advice
in the LERM Assembler manual to
use the system heap area from
16384 to store short bits of
code does not work with Master-
Basic.


Except for this problem, it is,
of course, possible to sense
whether or not MasterBasic is in
use by looking at DVAR 7 and
adapting a program to cover both
situations, as for example I
have done in Letta Checka(albeit
only to cover the enhanced CSIZE
command in MasterBasic).

I suspect that Mike Haine sent
you an early version of his
letter responding to my comments
on his KEYSET programs since we
have had a long correspondence
about things, and I believe that
we both now fully understand
each other's point of view.


A minor point, but I noticed a
small 'typing error' in my
comments on 'FORMAT without
VERIFY' - there is a reference
to 'on-zero' values, which
should of course be 'non-zero'.
I have checked that my Word-
Master file is correct - is this
just a slip of the Editor's
finger, or are there occasions
when you cannot read W/M files?

Further to Q and A on head
cleaners,have you ever published
a program to drive them? Their
use is not simple like a
cassette player cleaner, where
you 'play' in the normal way.
The one I use happens to have
come from FORMAT, and therefore
copyright, so I cannot send it
to you. If you haven't published
one, your readers might find one
useful.

I am still idly pursuing SNOS. I
tried...

  10 OPEN  #5, "n1"

   ...thinking you might need to
specify source (or destination)
number. SAMBASIC accepts it but
does not then recognise #5.

MASTERBASIC gives an error
message

  85 TRK - 68, SCT - 79, Error!!

I am baffled and have written
to Andy Wright.

        All best wishes,

           Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan D. Cox

The only information I have on
the control code CHR$ 9 is that
it turns a printer off-line. The
command doesn't work with my
humble Brother M1009 and neither
does it's opposite:CHR$ 17 which
is listed as "on-line". How it
can manage to send the code to
an off-line printer I do not
know! However, perhaps some new
printers have a pseudo off-line
mode which ignores everything
but CHR$ 17?

Regarding the reverse-listing
bug, I did as you suggested and
re-read your comments in Issue
54. I must be suffering from a
surfeit of info(OUTLET syndrome)
to have forgotten!

That also explains why I haven't
suffered from the problem as
much as others - because I am
frequently clearing the screen
before listing (one solution you
gave). This is because the BASIC
is slightly flawed (in my humble
opinion) because the PRINT posi-
tion marker is not moved to the
bottom of the screen properly
and it is most annoying to try
to print odd items such as quick
calculations only to find they
disappear somewhere in the list-
ing. The Spectrum never does
this. This also applies to LIST
of course and the top line of
the listing may be awkwardly
offset and hard to read. I have
long since added a CLS to the
LIST in function key F0.

Regarding editing errors, we can
convert any textfile that we
have so far seen but sometimes
our routines may space the
result out rather awkwardly and
subsequent editing may mistake
for example, "etc. .. n on-zero"
as a spurious n plus "on-zero".

You realize we have to employ
someone to edit letters, there
are a huge number - more than
any other SAM or Spectrum maga-
zine - and our typist is not
expert in computer terminology.
In addition, we get a very large
amount of letters with very poor
spelling, characters missing,
ambiguous wording etc. and it is
often hard to tell such errors
from conversion oddities!

I have never really reflected on
disc cleaner software. I guess
they must be written is machine
code and address the drive dir-
ectly.

Finally, Malcolm Perry's letter
has info about networking. Now,
here's Brian Gaff's comments on
the SAM disc controller...
            --------        B.C.
After a glance at the SAM
Technical manual, I have come to
the conclusion that yours is
different to mine! I have no
data sheet in mine!

I can comment about the 5.25"
drive reference though. In fact,
the index pulses are generated
by 3.5" drives. The chip could

not care less what is on the end
of it, as long as it obeys the
signals sent to it, and sends
back the data required. You can
even hang a 3" drive on the end,
if you want to.

It is the index pulses that have
caused the problems with
Masterdos and the newer 2Mb
drives SAMCO have been using.
The older drives gave pulses as
soon as the disc started to
turn, whereas, the new drives
only send them when the disc
speed is correct. This means
that when the older versions of
Masterdos are used with a new
drive, the DOS cannot see the
pulses, and stops with the Check
disc in drive error. Thankfully,
Andy Wright has fixed this now.

As for the address lines used, I
must admit that I have not
delved that deep. It would not
surprise me though, if the Tech
manual had an error here, as
many exist. The one I fell over
was the missing keyboard port,
65534. This reads the cursors
are CNTRL.

Getting back to the disc Verify
for a moment, this seems to just
read the track and sector
markers on the disc. You can
still have a sector that will
corrupt data, even when this
test is passed. Dave Tonks once
described the Verify as 'About
as useful as a chocolate
fire guard'!              B.G.

From: Kevin Cooper, CARLISLE

Dear Brian,

I enclosed Issue 54. The metal
shutter on the top of the disk
won't spring shut, could you
please sort it out? This leads
me onto my next point - the Post
Office. I'm fairly sure this is
to do with the P.O. If you look
carefully on the back of the
shutter it is slightly dented.

I seem to be having problems
with the P.O. recently. In
December, Derek Morgan sent me a
letter which never arrived, then
I received a letter the other
day asking why I hadn't replied
to somebody's letter - I didn't
receive it!

Then, of course, the Order for
OUTLET Issue No. 54, sent off a
couple of months ago, which you
didn't receive. The P.O. were
only supposed to have lost two
letters this Christmas!

In reply to Malcolm Perry: I
have had quite a few problems
with my SAM over the past few
months. It started in October
last year when my drive started
to play up. It was sent back
several times, then it seemed to
be okay, but I discoverd I was
getting the elusive "Check disk
in drive" error when using
Masterdos.

Then, it all started again -
drive 2 started going weird.

SAMCO decided to replace my SAM,
for which I'm grateful. I got a
512k model - mine was originally
a 256k version. Then problems
started immediately - the SAM
started to knock itself off! The
power pack was making too much
noise. Again, I contacted SAMCO.
I was told to send the PSU back,
and they would send a new one by
return post. (I have heard that
before and had to wait for
weeks!) Before I sent it, my dad
took a look. It turned out to be
two components on the side which
weren't connected (summat- or-
other-resistors) which take the
heat and pass it on to a metal
plate which allows the PSU to
cool down. So, because they
weren't connected, it wasn't
cooling down.

Everything seemed okay, until
the other day I disc-overed
(Yes, I know, crap Pun) that
with Masterdos I was sometimes
getting "Check Disk In Drive" on
drive 2, but on trying the same
disk operation again, without
doing anything beforehand - it
would work!So I've just left it.
Even if it is the drives (there
are other people with drive
problems) - remember, SAMCO buy
the drives from Citizen, so they
aren't to blame, unless it is
the SAM itself.

I also noticed the 'Format bit'
Malcolm mentioned on Masterdos.
I found sometimes it wouldn't
give the prompt "Are You Sure?",
and sometimes it would pause
before a Format.

Now and again it would be the
"Check disk..." error. I never
got it formatting with write
protect on though. It doesn't
seem to be just with Masterdos
though. Now and again when
copying a disk with a utility
that uses Samdos, drive 2 would
get the "Check disk..." error.

I also got the Primus issue 1
(double disk issue), for only a
quid, which seems excellent
value for money. I don't know
about the February issue though,
I sent an order off for it
months ago and haven't received
anything yet. I need to write.

My sister was pleased when she
saw her picccy on the title
screen! [OUTLET 55]

P.S. I've just realised I forgot
to post this letter and now have
an update about Primus magazine.
Nayur Khan, the person who runs
it, called me yesterday. He got
my letter about me not receiving
Primus 2, and called to explain.
He has got exams at the moment,
so it will be delayed. He said
he wrote a couple of weeks ago
explaining this. You guessed it,
I never received it! So, I
called the local Royal Mail
Customer Care unit. I explained
about four letters getting lost
in the post in the last four
months. Colin, (the person I was
talking to) said something was
obviously going wrong, and he
said to write to them with
details, addresses etc., so you
might get a letter any day now.

Brian Cavers to Kevin Cooper

You realize that if you write to
the Post Office with details
about letters getting lost in
the post that your letter may...
get lost in the post!

Regarding drive problems, I have
mentioned before that my drive 2
keeps "hanging up". This usually
happens at an awkard moment. DIR
2 sometimes clears it but not
always. A couple of days ago I
switched Drive 1 to 2. I thought
if it's going to hang it only
does it once in a reset so as
Drive 1 I would know immediately
and simply reset and start again
- more convenient than finding
out in the middle of a complex
operation using Drive 2!

Anyway, it seems a lot better
and in fact, as Drive 1 it is
not hanging up like it did as
Drive 2. I used to get several
hang-ups a day but so far, as
Drive 1 I have only had one
oddity and I think that may have
been something else because I
had already used the drive since
resetting.

Of course, I may simply have got
the drives seated better in the
sockets by chance. I'm sure I
tried this switch-over idea some
while ago without success but it
may have been different drives
or possibly in those days I did
not know you need to hold reset
for a couple of seconds or more
to make sure!

Our latest on the hardware front
is that we have had our 512K SAM
in for repair for 3 months now,
awaiting a new drive and are
unable to contact PBT by phone
or letter! If anyone can reach
them tell 'em we're desparate!

In addition, the SAM we borrowed
from a relative to keep us going
while the 512K was being fixed
has now broken down! The screen
is entirely black although one
can hear drive operations and
sound is normal.


Our one remaining SAM, mine, is
all that is keeping OUTLET going
so everybody keep their fingers
crossed!

Yes, I liked the SNOOPY picture
and it was just crying out to be
animated! I wish I had more time
to do more complicated cartoons
like that; they're good fun.

                        - Brian.

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Regarding the query from S.Glenn
about making a single drive re-
spond as drive 2, I take it his
question relates to using two
single drives as a duel drive
system or adding a second drive
to an existing single drive.

First a bit of general info: the
+D has a single connector that
carries all the data lines, side
select, write protect, read or
write and etc. These are common
to to both drives. The connector
also carries two additional
signals that decide if the
interface wants to use drive 1
or 2. These are separate on pins
10 and 12.

D1 or D2 select also go to both
drives so the drive needs to
know which it is supposed to be
and act upon. While the data and
etc. signals also go to both
drives they are only processed
if the drive has been selected
apart from the 'motor on' signal
which, in many drives, starts up
the motor if there is a disc in
the drive even if it has not
been selected.


In the drive itself there is
either a link or switch that
connects the appropiate D1 , D2
signal to the drive circuits.
Therefore, this switch/link
decides if it is drive 1 or 2.

However,to confuse matters,these
are often marked 0 & 1 (and
sometimes go on to 2 & 3) where
0 relates to D1 and 1 is D2 (2
makes it D3 and 3 for D4 which
+D does not use).

Two single drives can be used by
means of a 2-way adaptor that
plugs into the +D and has 2
sockets for the drives. These
seem to be advertised in BBC
computer mags more often.


There are in fact two types of
adaptor available. One is a
straight pin for pin connection
and each drive has to have its
internal link or switch
correctly set.

The second type of adaptor has
the drive signals crossed over
between the drive connectors
which means that both drives are
set as D1 but each receive the
correct D1 or D2 signal. This
later type of connector avoids
having to open up the drive to
change links to make it respond
as D2.

The UNIVERSAL drive sold by EEC
Ltd (the drive previously sold
by MGT as "Lifetime Drive" has
these drive select brought out
externally I understand. If
anyone is technically minded the
drive select can easily be
brought out to a switch as I
have done on a 3.5"and a 5.25"so
the combination can have either
drive D1/d2.

I can confirm both the sector
copy programs work ok on my Dis-
ciple that were stated as giving
sector error reports - both as
single- and dual-drive copy.

I recently had a word processor
PC brought to me by a friend who
said it would not work to drive
2. It turned out to be simply a
dirty connector to D2. (A repair
firm had previously charged `25
to "repair" this fault).

However, the point is, I was
told the computer cost some `500
and the PROGRAM was another
`500. The handbook was massive
but unhelpful! I.e., looking up
"drive problems" told you to
"read the instructions".

I suppose it is what you get
used to but on loading the
program the mass of information
put on screen was overwhelming
and did more to confuse than
help. It took about 1/2 hour to
find out how to select drive 2,
another 1/2 hour how to format a
disc and only 15 mins how to CAT
a disc as examples.

In fact it took about 1 1/2
hours just to find out how to
simply call on D2 to check for
the problem then 5 min to clear
the fault.

As for actually saving text to
disc after writing a file was
more like an adventure game to
get to do the actual SAVE.

If used daily it probably is all
quite simple but it certainly
made me realise how user-
friendly my Spectrum and SAM WP
progams are - not to mention the
difference in cost.

PCB DESIGNER.
I have the Disciple version and
confirm it gives satisfactory
printouts. However, the program
is written for different systems
and it seems is customised to
each system. That must be stated
on ordering. The handbook states
that each version requires a
different printer driver pro-
gram. The interface the writer
mentions is listed separately to
+D so obviously reason for
problem.

The printer routine is a separ-
ate program that is loaded as
required: a BASIC part under the
name "PRINTER" and a MC section
under the name "DP". I'd guess
that "DP" is the routine giving
the problems as the BASIC is
easily entered and the handbook
gives some code changes for such
as printers that do not accept
certain codes and etc.

The program was supplied on tape
to transfer to your own system
medium irrespective of version
ordered.I'd have thought Kemsoft
would have been prepared to
upgrade the printer driver for a
nominal charge if the system is
changed as "good customer
relations" not have to bear full
cost for a complete new program.

OMNICALC 2. There have been some
comments recently about this
program. However, I wonder if
there are different versions
floating around as Brian
mentioned he had broken into the
BASIC. I have both the tape
version that also does an auto
save to MD if it is connected
and a Disciple version on disc.

The first thing that was found
was that there simply is not any
BASIC program as such when it
first loads. The BASIC program
is simply 1 line containing the
whole of the program as MC. This
line is an auto run and the
first statement is a RANDOMISE
USR call to some 40 bytes
further along the line.

I then found that this line and
USR basic is overwritten with
more MC once the program
autoruns.

I did start to compare the
Disciple version and the tape
version but the program had
considerable differences from
the start so I did not pursue
the matter.

However, it is worth mentioning
that the Disciple version seems
to retain all the original tape
functions and the disc and
printer extensions are entered
via an additional menu called by
"z" command. Even on first
loading the disc version will
revert to tape function if not
careful.

I suspect, therefore, that the
+D version is the standard
tape/MD with the +D extention
added in as an extra bit of
code.

I did not have any luck in
"fooling" the system to think it
had a MD connected either with
the routine mentioned in OUTLET.


To follow up a couple of
previous comments about problem
using it with a Disciple giving
crashes and resets: I had no
difficulty with a "snap" SAVE to
disc and reLOADing of the tape
version - also the normal screen
printout seems to work ok for me
via the Disciple.

In response to all the queries
about a spelling checker program
it may be of interest that there
is one on the ENCELADUS #9 disc
that does work with OUTWRITE
files. Its dictionary is some-
what limited but it's intended
more for the user to build up
their own dictionary file as
they go along by adding words as
required.

                Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Thanks, Malcolm.

I've just come across another
printed letter of yours of which
I seem to have mislaid the text
file. Sorry I'm too late to fit
it in but basically you say that
OMNICALC 2 works with SPECLONE
from Steve's Software. Printer
functions work with the SAM but
save is to tape only.
                       - Brian

From: Marc Broster,
      11 Church  Road,
      Saxilby, Lincs, LN1 2HH

Dear Brian,

Thanks for taking the time to
reply to my letter in the April
ish, yes, okay, I did ask you
for your opinion, so I should
have 'Let it lie'. Not wishing
to dwell on the subject, but
I've just got hold of a copy of
the Worm demo from ish 47. Er,
is it just me, or isn't the demo
total crap?

Okay, it was your compo, so you
have the right to judge it, but
come-on, it looks like something
which has been dredged up from
Fastline disk 7.

Not to discourage Matthew, this
time last year I was writing
similar stuff, but the prog has
had about as much time spent
polishing it up as I spend
reading 'Anorak Weekly', i.e.
none at all. It's not that I
mind losing. If I was judging, I
would send the money to Edwin
Blink, for his great Def Leppard
sample demo, which I belive you
published in ish 49. Could you
tell me why you thought so
highly of Matthew's demo?

You may be interested to know I
am writing a version of Columns,
a Tetris-type game, for the SAM.
The program is still in its
early stages, but it should be
quite good. More details as it
progresses.

Finally, you made the point in
your reply that ideas are much
more important than programming
skill, which is true, for things
like films or books, but not so
justified for computer games.

Admittedly, most new games have
some new twist which makes them
different, for example the two
characters in 'Head over Heels'
but that's nothing Earth
shattering. The general theme to
H.O.H. had been seen several
times before.

Okay, so from time to time you
get games like Elite or Tetris,
but I would be surprised if you
could name ten games which have
had new gamestyles.

What made 'Head over Heels'so
good, and what makes great games
like 'Sonic the Hegdehog' on the
MegaDrive outstanding is that
care has been taken to carefully
design the levels so monsters
and puzzles come at just the
right time, and frustrating 'Go
back to the start' or 'Practic-
ally impossible' sections are
ironed out.

However, to make a really good
game, graphics, sprite movement,
special effects and sound are
also needed.

This is probably more apparent
on the Megadrive than on the
Spectrum,where,as you said, most
games have a similar quality of

programming, but without the
amazing graphics, incredibly
trendy soundtracks, and shocking
specal effects that goes into
'Sonic'or my current fave 'The
Revenge of Shinobi' many Mega-
Drive games, even though they
have well thought out game-play,
are dull and uninteresting.

          Best Wishes,

         Marc Broster

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster

Our reasons for judging Matthew
Weedall's the best entry were
given with the announcement of
the winner in the Issue 54 edit-
orial, namely...

"The demo showed more innovation
and imagination than any other.
True,it has some rough spots and
more care could have been taken
with exactly matching positions
on-screen but overall it is the
most original, different and
humorous!"

Your examples of HEAD OVER HEELS
etc. support my previous claim
that the ideas (meaning the game
design) are more important than

Following my query recently about the use of CHR$(19) with the Tandy CGP-115, I received a very helpful letter from Dr. Tom Wilson of Falkirk and we sub- sequently spoke on the phone. I've been driving the CGP using my EPSON HX20, partly because it seemed appropriate to couple together two contemporary pieces

I suggested to him that he would do better using the parallel port (with a printer switch if he wanted to keep the CGP and his LC-20 connected up at the same time). This proved OK, but in the process I also found that using SAM, and this interface, with SAM BASIC, I did not need CHR$(19) in order to get proper output!

So where am I? Is it that CHR$(19) is something to do with driving the serial input to the CGP? or is it something to do with EPSON/Microsoft BASIC? I have written to Tandy, who are normally very helpful in response to problems such as this, and they say that they are as baffled as I am. Following their suggestion, I have written to Radio Shack/Tandy in the USA: I will, of course, let you know if this resolves the problem.

Thank you for your comments on OUTDEX and SC_ASSEMBLER in this month's OUTLET. I will follow up your suggestions - which I am sure others will also find useful - and let you know in due

course whether I have been successful (and it is no good making remarks like 'as clever as you' - I do not respond to such blatant flattery!). I note that you offer no comments on the apparent misinformation on the disk controller in SAM - has Brian Gaff any comments?

After a glance at the SAM Technical manual, I have come to the conclusion that yours is different to mine! I have no data sheet in mine!

I can comment about the 5.25" drive reference though. In fact, the index pulses are generated by 3.5" drives. The chip could

not care less what is on the end of it, as long as it obeys the signals sent to it, and sends back the data required. You can even hang a 3" drive on the end, if you want to.

It is the index pulses that have caused the problems with Masterdos and the newer 2Mb drives SAMCO have been using. The older drives gave pulses as soon as the disc started to turn, whereas, the new drives only send them when the disc speed is correct. Regarding the query from S.Glenn about making a single drive re- spond as drive 2, I take it his question relates to using two single drives as a duel drive system or adding a second drive to an existing single drive.

First a bit of general info: the +D has a single connector that carries all the data lines, side select, write protect, read or write and etc. These are common to to both drives. The connector also carries two additional signals that decide if the interface wants to use drive 1 or 2. These are separate on pins 10 and 12.

D1 or D2 select also go to both drives so the drive needs to know which it is supposed to be and act upon. While the data and etc. signals also go to both drives they are only processed if the drive has been selected apart from the 'motor on' signal which, in many drives, starts up the motor if there is a disc in the drive even if it has not been selected.

In the drive itself there is either a link or switch that connects the appropiate D1 , D2 signal to the drive circuits. Therefore, this switch/link decides if it is drive 1 or 2.

However,to confuse matters,these are often marked 0 & 1 (and sometimes go on to 2 & 3) where 0 relates to D1 and 1 is D2 (2 makes it D3 and 3 for D4 which +D does not use).

Two single drives can be used by means of a 2-way adaptor that plugs into the +D and has 2 sockets for the drives. These seem to be advertised in BBC computer mags more often.

There are in fact two types of adaptor available. One is a straight pin for pin connection and each drive has to have its internal link or switch correctly set.

The second type of adaptor has the drive signals crossed over between the drive connectors which means that both drives are set as D1 but each receive the correct D1 or D2 signal. This later type of connector avoids having to open up the drive to change links to make it respond as D2.

The UNIVERSAL drive sold by EEC Ltd (the drive previously sold by MGT as "Lifetime Drive" has these drive select brought out externally I understand. If anyone is technically minded the drive select can easily be brought out to a switch as I have done on a 3.5"and a 5.25"so the combination can have either drive D1/d2.

I can confirm both the sector copy programs work ok on my Dis- ciple that were stated as giving sector error reports - both as single- and dual-drive copy.

I recently had a word processor PC brought to me by a friend who said it would not work to drive 2. It turned out to be simply a dirty connector to D2. (A repair firm had previously charged `25 to "repair" this fault).

However, the point is, I was told the computer cost some `500 and the PROGRAM was another `500. The handbook was massive but unhelpful! I.e., looking up "drive problems" told you to "read the instructions".

I suppose it is what you get used to but on loading the program the mass of information put on screen was overwhelming and did more to confuse than help. It took about 1/2 hour to find out how to select drive 2, another 1/2 hour how to format a disc and only 15 mins how to CAT a disc as examples.

In fact it took about 1 1/2 hours just to find out how to simply call on D2 to check for the problem then 5 min to clear the fault.

As for actually saving text to disc after writing a file was more like an adventure game to get to do the actual SAVE.

If used daily it probably is all quite simple but it certainly made me realise how user- friendly my Spectrum and SAM WP progams are - not to mention the difference in cost.

PCB DESIGNER. I have the Disciple version and confirm it gives satisfactory printouts. However, the program is written for different systems and it seems is customised to each system. That must be stated on ordering. The handbook states that each version requires a different printer driver pro- gram. The interface the writer mentions is listed separately to +D so obviously reason for problem.

The printer routine is a separ- ate program that is loaded as required: a BASIC part under the name "PRINTER" and a MC section under the name "DP". I'd guess that "DP" is the routine giving the problems as the BASIC is easily entered and the handbook gives some code changes for such as printers that do not accept certain codes and etc.

The program was supplied on tape to transfer to your own system medium irrespective of version ordered.I'd have thought Kemsoft would have been prepared to upgrade the printer driver for a nominal charge if the system is changed as "good customer relations" not have to bear full cost for a complete new program.

OMNICALC 2. There have been some comments recently about this program. However, I wonder if there are different versions floating around as Brian mentioned he had broken into the BASIC. I have both the tape version that also does an auto save to MD if it is connected and a Disciple version on disc.

The first thing that was found was that there simply is not any BASIC program as such when it first loads. The BASIC program is simply 1 line containing the whole of the program as MC. This line is an auto run and the first statement is a RANDOMISE USR call to some 40 bytes further along the line.

I then found that this line and USR basic is overwritten with more MC once the program autoruns.

I did start to compare the Disciple version and the tape version but the program had considerable differences from the start so I did not pursue the matter.

However, it is worth mentioning that the Disciple version seems to retain all the original tape functions and the disc and printer extensions are entered via an additional menu called by "z" command. Even on first loading the disc version will revert to tape function if not careful.

I suspect, therefore, that the +D version is the standard tape/MD with the +D extention added in as an extra bit of code.

In response to all the queries about a spelling checker program it may be of interest that there is one on the ENCELADUS #9 disc that does work with OUTWRITE files. Its dictionary is some- what limited but it's intended more for the user to build up their own dictionary file as they go along by adding words as required.

Сигналы выбора D1 или D2 также поступают на оба привода, поэтому дисковод должен «знать», кем он должен быть, и реагировать соответственно. Хотя данные и прочие сигналы идут на оба дисковода, они обрабатываются только в том случае, если дисковод выбран — за исключением сигнала «motor on», который во многих дисководах запускает мотор, если внутри есть диск, даже если сам дисковод не был выбран.

Внутри самого привода есть либо перемычка, либо переключатель, который подключает соответствующий сигнал D1/D2 к схемам дисковода. Таким образом, этот переключатель/перемычка и определяет, является ли он дисководом 1 или 2.

Однако, чтобы всё запутать, они часто маркируются как 0 и 1 (а иногда дело доходит до 2 и 3), где 0 соответствует D1, а 1 — это D2 (2 делает его D3, а 3 — D4, которые интерфейс +D не использует).

Два отдельных дисковода можно использовать с помощью переходника-разветвителя, который подключается к +D и имеет 2 разъёма для дисководов. Похоже, такие штуки чаще рекламируются в журналах по компьютерам BBC.

На самом деле существует два типа таких адаптеров. Первый — с прямым соединением «контакт-в-контакт», где на каждом дисководе нужно правильно выставить внутреннюю перемычку или переключатель.

Второй тип адаптера имеет перекрещенные сигналы выбора дисковода между разъёмами, а это значит, что оба привода настроены как D1, но каждый из них получает правильный сигнал D1 или D2. Этот второй тип разъёма избавляет от необходимости вскрывать дисковод и переставлять перемычки, чтобы заставить его отвечать как D2.

Насколько я понимаю, в дисководе UNIVERSAL от EEC Ltd (ранее продававшемся компанией MGT под названием «Lifetime Drive») этот переключатель выбора дисковода выведен наружу. Если кто-то дружит с паяльником, выбор привода можно легко вывести на тумблер, как я и сделал на своих 3.5" и 5.25" дисководах, так что в этой связке любой дисковод может быть D1 или D2.

Могу подтвердить, что обе программы посекторного копирования, о которых писали, будто они выдают ошибки секторов, отлично работают на моём Disciple — как в однодисководном, так и в двухдисководном режиме.

Недавно друг принёс мне текстовый процессор на базе PC, сказав, что он не работает с дисководом 2. Оказалось, дело было просто в грязном разъёме D2. (А ведь ремонтная фирма до этого содрала с него £25 за «устранение» этой неисправности).

Впрочем, суть в том, что, как мне сказали, компьютер стоил около £500, и ПРОГРАММА — ещё £500. Руководство пользователя было толстенным, но совершенно бесполезным! Например, в разделе «проблемы с дисководом» советовалось «прочитать инструкцию».

### PCB DESIGNER

У меня версия для Disciple, и я подтверждаю, что она даёт удовлетворительную печать. Однако программа написана под разные системы и, похоже, индивидуально настраивается под каждую из них. Это необходимо указывать при заказе. В руководстве указано, что для каждой версии требуется свой драйвер принтера. Интерфейс, о котором упоминает автор письма, указан отдельно от +D, так что причина проблемы очевидна.

Подпрограмма печати представляет собой отдельную программу, которая загружается по мере необходимости: часть на Бейсике под названием «PRINTER» и блок в машинных кодах под названием «DP». Полагаю, проблемы вызывает именно «DP», поскольку Бейсик легко посмотреть и отредактировать, а в руководстве приведены некоторые изменения кода для случаев, когда принтер не воспринимает определённые управляющие коды и т.д.

Программа поставлялась на кассете для последующего переноса на носитель вашей системы, независимо от заказанной версии. Я думаю, что Kemsoft могла бы пойти навстречу и обновить драйвер принтера за символическую плату в случае смены системы — просто из соображений «хороших отношений с клиентами», чтобы человеку не приходилось оплачивать полную стоимость совершенно новой программы.

### OMNICALC 2

В последнее время было несколько отзывов об этой программе. Однако мне интересно, не гуляют ли по рукам разные её версии, ведь Brian упомянул, что он прервал выполнение и залез в Бейсик. У меня есть как кассетная версия (которая также делает автосохранение на микродрайв, если он подключён), так и дисковая версия для Disciple.

Первое, что выяснилось: при начальной загрузке там попросту нет никакой Бейсик-программы как таковой. Вся программа на Бейсике — это всего 1 строка, содержащая всю программу в виде машинного кода. Эта строка настроена на автозапуск, и первым оператором идёт вызов `RANDOMIZE USR` примерно на 40 байт дальше по строке.

Затем я обнаружил, что эта строка и бейсиковский USR перезаписываются новым машинным кодом, как только программа автоматически запускается.

Я начал было сравнивать версию для Disciple и кассетную версию, но в программе с самого начала обнаружились значительные различия, поэтому я не стал продолжать.

Однако стоит отметить, что версия для Disciple, похоже, сохраняет все оригинальные кассетные функции, а расширения для диска и принтера открываются через дополнительное меню, вызываемое командой «z». Даже при первой загрузке дисковая версия норовит переключиться на работу с кассетой, если не быть осторожным.

Поэтому я подозреваю, что версия для +D — это стандартный вариант tape/MD, в который просто добавили немного кода расширения под +D.

Мне также не удалось «обмануть» систему, заставив её думать, что подключён микродрайв, с помощью процедуры, описанной в OUTLET.

В продолжение пары предыдущих комментариев о проблемах при использовании с интерфейсом Disciple (зависания и сбросы): у меня не возникло никаких трудностей со «snap»-сохранением (SAVE) на диск и последующей загрузкой (LOAD) кассетной версии — обычная печать экрана через Disciple у меня тоже работает нормально.

В ответ на все запросы касательно программы проверки орфографии: возможно, вам будет интересно узнать, что на диске ENCELADUS #9 есть такая программа, и она работает с файлами OUTWRITE. Словарь у неё несколько ограничен, но она больше рассчитана на то, чтобы пользователь сам пополнял свой файл словаря в процессе работы, добавляя нужные слова по мере необходимости.
